packet.claim: The documented parsing rule fails to correctly recover JSON objects when they appear inside a fenced code block that also contains surrounding prose, causing an INVALID_INSTANTIATION error.
packet.expected: The rule should allow recovery of a top‑level JSON object from within a fence even when additional text precedes or follows it, and should not raise an INVALID_INSTANTIATION.
packet.observed: INVALID_INSTANTIATION: 'the input is not the cell it names: MINI_USETEST_CELL_UNREADABLE: 'fence[ {"a":1} ] Here is the result:' names '{"a":1}', which the grammar does not hold'
packet.scope: JSON objects embedded in fenced code blocks that are not the sole content of the cell (i.e., surrounded by additional prose).
packet.source_basis: Every top‑level balanced object in the text is a candidate, not only the span from the first ``{`` to the last ``}``: reasoning prose before or after the answer frequently contains stray braces, and an object nested inside another is not a candidate of its own.
packet.uncertainty: Whether the rule intends to accept any surrounding prose or only when the fence itself contains the object, and whether the error stems from the grammar or the test harness.
